purpose: Define the separation between canonical namespace existence, configured capability availability, mounted availability and active runtime state.

topics.name: Namespace Availability and Lifecycle
topics.purpose: Define the separation between canonical namespace existence, configured capability availability, mounted availability and active runtime state.

semantics.existence_rule: A reserved root may exist canonically even when its optional subsystem is unavailable or inactive.
semantics.configuration_rule: Configured capability does not automatically imply mounted or active runtime state.
semantics.mount_rule: Mount availability is runtime/configuration state and does not redefine namespace identity.
semantics.active_rule: Active service/module state is separate from namespace definition.
semantics.disable_rule: Disabling optional capability removes availability but not the canonical reserved-root definition where that root remains reserved.
semantics.introspection_rule: Introspection exposes both canonical definition and current availability state distinctly.

invariants.rule: Every active reserved runtime root has exactly one explicit owner contract and remains distinguishable from runtime availability, Topic grouping and physical implementation location.

hard_gates.condition: disabled subsystem deletes reserved root identity
configured state conflated with active state
mount state becomes semantic namespace identity
availability state inferred only from file presence
introspection cannot distinguish definition from runtime availability

prose.summary: Define the separation between canonical namespace existence, configured capability availability, mounted availability and active runtime state.
